pages.title: Stado overview
pages.description: What Stado is and how work moves through its queue.

claim.evidence: policy-controlled queue and compute control plane

blocks.text: Stado is a policy-controlled queue and compute control plane: you hand it a job, and it dispatches that job to a worker under the policies you set.
These docs were verified against stado 0.7.9.

sections.title: How work moves through the queue

items: submit — Submit a job (or batch) to the queue.
queue — Maintenance mode: pause/resume dispatching, and drain the fleet.

blocks.text: Maintenance mode never kills work: pausing stops dispatching and claiming, and jobs already claimed finish untouched.

claim.evidence: `config init` never overwrites an existing file

blocks.text: config init prints the path to the new $HOME/.stado/config.json and never overwrites an existing file.

code.label: shell
code.code:

stado status <job-id>
stado results <job-id> ./stado-result

claim.evidence: status progresses from queued or running to completed

blocks.text: The status progresses from queued or running to completed, and the downloaded output contains hello from Stado.

pages.title: stado queue
pages.description: Maintenance mode: pause or resume dispatching, and drain the fleet.

claim.evidence: Maintenance mode: pause/resume dispatching, and drain the fleet

blocks.text: stado queue owns maintenance mode for the fleet: it can pause or resume dispatching, and drain running work to zero.

claim.evidence: Stop dispatching and claiming; running jobs finish untouched

table.caption: stado queue subcommands
rows: Stop dispatching and claiming; running jobs finish untouched
Pause state plus how much work is queued and still running
Pause, then (with --wait) block until no job is running any more

claim.evidence: Wait for running/ to empty instead of returning immediately
Exits non-zero if it elapses with jobs still running [default: 900]

blocks.text: --timeout is the deadline for --wait, in seconds; drain exits non-zero if the deadline elapses with jobs still running. The default is 900 seconds.

callout.title: Running jobs are safe
callout.text: Pausing stops dispatching and claiming only; running jobs finish untouched.
